name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 4, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the
City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:00 p.m., on April
4, 2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 30, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:02 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Ury
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Reardon

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor
  Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the

City Council Minutes  1  April 4, 2011
   Negotiations are the City and the City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's
  Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiator pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.8. Property is an approximate 7.12 acre site generally located at the
  intersection of Oso Parkway and Montanoso Drive, adjacent to Mission Viejo
  Country Club and owned by Watermarke Properties, Inc./Mission Viejo Club
  Apartments, LLC ("Watermarke"). CDA Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, City
  Manager/CDA Executive Director, Charles Wilson, Director of Community
  Development, James Williams, Economic Advisor, Celeste Brady, CDA Counsel,
  and William Curley, III, Esq., City Attorney. Owner's Negotiators: Greg Neville of
  Watermarke and Jeffrey M. Oderman of Rutan & Tucker, Counsel to Owner.
  Under negotiation: potential acquisition and/or disposition of real property
  interests for long term affordable housing and the price and terms of payment
  therefore related to the above-listed property. Factors affecting price and terms
  under negotiation: recorded covenants, scope of development of property, and
  affordable housing requirements. Factors affecting time of payment: conditions to
  closing, due diligence period, and schedule of development of affordable housing.

CS3. Conference with Real Property Negotiator pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.8. Property is an approximate 10.5 acre Site commonly referred to as the
  "Former K Mart" located at 28601 Los Alisos Boulevard and Comprised of
  Assessor Parcel Nos. (APNs) 839-161-08 and 839-161-09 owned by Union Dominion
  Realty/Pacific Los Alisos L.P. ("UDR"). CDA negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, City
  Manager/CDA Executive Director, Charles Wilson, Director of Community
  Development, James Williams, Economic Advisor, Celeste Brady, CDA Counsel,
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney. Owner's negotiators: Jeremy Cyr of UDR
  and John Ramirez, Kerra Carlson of Rutan & Tucker, Frank Spevacek of Rosenow
  Spevacek Group, ad Peter Whittingham of Curt Pringle Associates, all on behalf of
  UDR. Under negotiation: potential acquisition and/or disposition of real property
  interests for long term affordable housing and the price and terms of payment
  therefore related to the above-listed property. Factors affecting price and terms
  under negotiation: recorded covenants, scope of development of property,
  affordable housing requirements. Factors affecting time of payment: conditions to
  closing, due diligence period, and schedule of development and development of
  affordable housing.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:08 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Council Minutes  2  April 4, 2011
 City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council considered items CS2 and CS3 in Closed
Session. By unanimous vote, the City Council provided instruction and direction to staff but
there was no reportable action. The City Council will reconvene in Closed Session at the end of
the meeting to consider item CS1.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adoptable Pets of the Month

  Mayor Leckness highlighted four animals available for adoption at the Mission Viejo
  Animal Services Center.

P2.  Presentation by the Sierra Club’s Orange County Global Warming Committee
  Recognizing the City of Mission Viejo’s Recent Installation of a Photo Voltaic
  "Solar" Powered System on the Roof of City Hall

  On behalf of the Sierra Club, Laura Jackson recognized the City for its newly solar
  powered city hall building and she presented Mayor Leckness with a solar powered decal.

P3.  2011 Community Opinion Survey

  Dr. Timothy McLarney, President of True North Research, presented the 2011
  Community Opinion Survey results.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: expressed disappointment that Mayor Leckness did not read his email
message, in its entirety, during the City Council Meetings on March 7 and March 21, 2011.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, and 7 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  3  April 4, 2011
 1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of March 21, 2011, as
  presented.

5.  Check Register dated March 18, 2011, in the amount of $810,425.95

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  American Recovery & Reinvestment Act of 2009 (ARRA) - Energy Efficient Light
  Fixtures and Bulb Replacements at the Norman P. Murray Community & Senior
  Center, Civic Center, and City Traffic Signals - Yellow (CIP 320)

  Approved the agreement for subject project to Republic ITS, in an amount not to exceed
  $165,840.00.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Summary of FY 2010-11 Budget Amendments To Date

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about damages related to 2010 winter storms as listed
  on page 2 of the report. She asked if the City has made $31,250 in repairs.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein responded
  that the number listed is a net of the $500,000 included in the amended budget to address
  storm damages, less the amount of reimbursement the City received from the Federal and
  State governments. The net draw on the General Fund is the difference between those
  two, or $31,000.

City Council Minutes  4  April 4, 2011
   Council Member Schlicht asked when the City will start spending these monies on storm
  repairs.

  City Manager Wilberg announced that some of the repairs have already been made, for
  example, fallen trees were addressed during and shortly after the storm. The major
  portion of work that remains are creek repairs and staff is in the process of obtaining bids
  for that work.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to receive
  and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

4.  Check Register dated March 11, 2011, in the amount of $1,253,032.23

  Council Member Reardon inquired about payments made to Amerinational Community
  Services, Friess Construction, and Jamey Clark, Inc.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein described
  the services that these contractors provide for the City.

  Council Member Reardon inquired about over-billing for City Attorney services.

  Mr. Curley described that coding for one of the attorneys was not changed to the lower
  Assistant City Attorney rate. Administrative Services staff caught the error, a correction
  has been made and a credit has been provided.

  Mayor Leckness inquired about graffiti removal.

  Public Services Operations Manager Jerry Hill described the mechanisms that staff has in
  place for inspection and removal of graffiti.

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment made to Webtrends, Inc.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein responded
  that the company provides the City with web site usage numbers.

City Council Minutes  5  April 4, 2011
   Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

7.  Designation of County Route S18 as the Orange County Deputy Sheriffs Memorial
  Highway

  Council Member Schlicht asked if this is a designation only or if the name of the street is
  being changed.

  City Manager Wilberg responded that it is a designation only.

  Council Member Reardon read the names of the Orange County Sheriffs Deputies who
  lost their lives in the line of duty.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 11-21 Officially Recognizing the Designation of County Route S18 as the
  Orange County Deputy Sheriffs Memorial Highway.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR'S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

8.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

9.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Ury presented the report.

10.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

City Council Minutes  6  April 4, 2011
   Mayor Leckness presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

11.  Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2010/11

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  details of the mid-year budget review for Fiscal Year 2010/11.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 11-22 Amending the FY 2010/11 Budget for Adjustments to Various
  Revenue and Expenditure Accounts.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Attorney’s Report

12.  Proposed Urgency Ordinance Amending Section 9.29.220 of the Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code Pertaining to Subdivision Sales and Model Home Directional Signs

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Urgency Ordinance 11-XXX Adopting Revisions to Short Term Signage and Use
  Standards.

  After discussion of the proposed ordinance, Mayor Pro Tem Ury withdrew his motion.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to (1) refer
  this matter to the Planning and Transportation Commission for review and comment; and
  (2) allow Lennar Homes to immediately proceed with its proposed signage (consistent
  with the proposed sign regulations outlined on pages 2 and 3 of the agenda report) for a
  maximum of 6 months, without enforcement or penalty. During this time the City will
  accept public input and will review the signage for consideration of a more permanent
  update to the City’s sign code.

City Council Minutes  7  April 4, 2011
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

13.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at recent events including Kristi Yamaguchi’s
appearance at the Murray Community Center, the Marine Adoption Committee golf tournament
which raised $21,000, a Persian New Year celebration at Comerica Bank, a Senior Summit
hosted by Supervisor Pat Bates, Mission Viejo Activities Committee’s brand new event, Up in
the Air, and the Nadadores awards banquet. Council Member Kelley announced that she will be
hosting a blood drive on April 19, 2011, from 2:00 to 4:00 p.m. at the Murray Community
Center. She also reminded residents that on April 23, the City will host Bunny Days on the
Village Green at Oso Viejo Park and Arts Alive festival from April 28 to May 1, 2011. Council
Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month of April is
service and the movie of character, Amazing Grace, will be shown on April 17, 2011, in the City
Council Chamber.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon discussed her recent activities including a tour of the City’s animal
shelter, a Cub Scout tour of city hall with staff member Karen Wylie, the Marine Adoption
Committee’s golf tournament, and a meeting with representatives of UDR. She and Council
Member Schlicht learned more about UDR’s proposed development at the former K-Mart site
and expressed their concerns about the density and recommended that the developer meet with
residents of Palmia to hear their concerns. Council Member Reardon also outlined her
attendance at a Regional Housing Needs Assessment discussion and meetings with the developer
Standard Pacific, Assembly Member Diane Harkey’s staff, and a Teen Challenge event. Council
Member Reardon concluded her comments by reminding her colleagues and residents to
continue praying for two young children who are fighting cancer.

City Council Minutes  8  April 4, 2011
 Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht discussed Teen Challenge and stated that the program is a faith-based
success story. Many people who complete the program give back by helping others. Council
Member Schlicht questioned Mayor Leckness’ water challenge and asked the City Attorney if he
can do this without Council authority.

City Attorney Curley indicated that he is not familiar with the challenge but he will follow-up
and provide a response.

Council Member Schlicht outlined recent meetings with Council Member Reardon and two
developers. They met with UDR and reiterated their concerns with proposed density and they
had a meeting with Standard Pacific to receive an update on the annexation process. Standard
Pacific hopes to return to the City with their annexation request in May. She also discussed her
meeting with Assemblywoman Diane Harkey’s staff where she learned what is happening in
Sacramento and she attended the Mission Viejo Activities Committee Up in the Air event.
Council Member Schlicht reminded residents that there will be a Tea Party rally on April 15,
2011, outside city hall from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m. and Congressman Gary Miller will visit the
Murray Community and Senior Center on April 21. She concluded her comments with a quote
from Abraham Lincoln, “Let us have faith that right makes might, and in that faith, let us, to the
end, dare to do our duty as we understand it” and from Benjamin Franklin, “man will ultimately
be governed by God or by tyrants.”

Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Ury stated that the Council needs to take a look at things and put them into
proper perspective. He noted that according to the recent Community Opinion Survey, Mission
Viejo residents appreciate their quality of life and the job the City Council and City staff are
doing. He noted that his colleague made what amounts to a legal challenge regarding Mayor
Leckness’ water conservation contest and once again, perspective is a healthy thing to have.
Mayor Pro Tem Ury announced that he had a great time at the Marine golf tournament and he
thanked the Marine Adoption Committee and City staff for a great event.

Mayor Leckness

Mayor Leckness outlined his attendance at recent events including a Kiwanis Club meeting, the
Capo Valley High School JV Soccer Banquet, police services’ Chili Cook Off in which he
participated as a judge, and a celebration before the commencement of the Portola horseback
ride. Mayor Leckness stated that the Council is bursting with pride over the Community Opinion
Survey results and he thanked City Manager Wilberg and City staff for working hard to make
sure that residents enjoy such a great quality of life. He asked Mr. Wilberg if the Council can

City Council Minutes  9  April 4, 2011
 honor staff in some way.

City Manger Wilberg noted that there is an annual Employee Recognition luncheon and this
year, the event will be held on May 6. He encouraged the City Council Members to attend.

Mayor Leckness invited residents to take the Mayor’s Water Challenge during the month of
April by visiting www.mywaterpledge.com and lastly, he encouraged residents to attend the Mad
Hatter Easter Tea Party at Kaleidoscope shopping center on April 16 from 10:00 a.m. to noon.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

Mayor Leckness declared a recess to Closed Session at 8:18 p.m. The City Council reconvened
at 9:58 p.m., with all five City Council Members present.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:00 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting to Monday, April 18, 2011, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 18, 2011

City Council Minutes  10  April 4, 2011
